annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and deterministic one-atom specialization of Theorem 3.6

assumptions: The truncation radius B is between zero and one.
Every finite relative-error factor has magnitude at most B.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p17_t1_product_bias_envelope (n : Nat) (B : Real) (hB0 : 0 <= B) (hB1 : B <= 1) (delta : Fin n -> Real) (hdelta : forall i, abs (delta i) <= B) : (1-B)^n <= product i, (1+delta i) and product i, (1+delta i) <= (1+B)^n
formal_statement.plain_language: A finite product of relative-error factors bounded by B lies between the lower and upper binomial envelopes from Theorem 3.6.

informal_proof: Each factor lies between 1-B and 1+B. Since B is at most one, the lower factors are nonnegative, so monotonicity of finite products gives both bounds.
informal_statement: The deterministic one-atom specialization of Theorem 3.6's expectation envelope for accumulated limited-precision stochastic-rounding errors.
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47(5), 2025, pages B1227-B1249

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen RoundingProductBounds module contains the same finite product envelope; the L proof is a direct application after paper-scoped renaming.

source_locations.anchor: completion of the induction proof and Remark 3.7 specialization

tier_rationale: The frozen theorem NumStability.prod_one_add_delta_bounds has the same product surface and conclusion. The L proof only supplies the paper-scoped names and hypotheses.
